message.content:
**Answer:**  
The most recent common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, a group of placental mammals that includes carnivores, ungulates, bats, and several other orders. This ancestor lived roughly 90–100 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.

**Why this is the common ancestor**

| Taxonomic level | Lion | Zebra | Last common ancestor |
|-----------------|------|-------|----------------------|
| Species | *Panthera leo* | *Equus quagga* | — |
| Genus | *Panthera* | *Equus* | — |
| Family | Felidae | Equidae | — |
| Order | Carnivora | Perissodactyla | — |
| Superorder | Euarchontoglires (no) | — | — |
| Clade | Laurasiatheria | Laurasiatheria | **Last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria** |

- **Felidae** (lions) belong to the order **Carnivora**.  
- **Equidae** (zebras) belong to the order **Perissodactyla**.  

Both orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains orders such as Artiodactyla (even‑toed ungulates), Chiroptera (bats), Cetartiodactyla (whales and hippos), and others. The last common ancestor of these two orders is therefore the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria.

**Timeframe**

Molecular clock estimates place the divergence of Laurasiatheria from other placental mammals at about 90–100 million years ago. Thus, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras would have been a small, likely insectivorous or omnivorous mammal living in the Late Cretaceous.

---

**Bottom line:** The lion and zebra share a common ancestor at the level of the clade Laurasiatheria, a placental mammal that existed around 90–100 million years ago.

That is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all mammals except monotremes and marsupials? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra would be the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. That is a mammal. So answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria, which is a placental mammal that lived around 90 million years ago. Alternatively, we can say that the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals.
